input:
This summary looks at a proposed heat-recovery retrofit at a food plant and at whether the project should move forward at this stage. The plant currently uses 2220 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration, which represents a substantial part of the site's overall energy picture. According to the equipment vendor, the retrofit is projected to save 14% of that electricity use, which works out to a derived saving of 311 MWh per year at the vendor figure. The capital cost of the retrofit is $370k. Using an electricity price of $0.09 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $28k, and the derived simple payback is 13.2 years.

It is important to note that the saving figure is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant, and that refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled either. Against that background, the recommendation is that the plant first carries out a metered trial on one of its three refrigeration lines before any capital decision is taken, so that the projected saving can be checked against actual operating experience. The plant engineer owns the trial.
target:
Recommendation: the plant runs a metered trial of the heat-recovery retrofit on one of its three refrigeration lines before any capital decision. The plant engineer owns the trial.

The case rests on a vendor projection, not on a measurement. The plant uses 2220 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration. The equipment vendor projects that the retrofit saves 14% of that use, a derived saving of 311 MWh per year at the vendor figure. Capital cost is $370k. At an electricity price of $0.09 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $28k and the derived simple payback is 13.2 years. A payback of that length, resting on an unmeasured saving, does not carry a capital decision on its own.

Two gaps stand in the evidence. The saving figure was not measured at this plant, and refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, so the projected saving has not been tested against the plant's highest-load conditions, which are the conditions under which refrigeration demand and the recovered heat are both at their most demanding. The metered trial closes the first gap on one line: it measures the saving where the retrofit would actually run, and it gives the plant a measured figure to set against the projected annual saving and the capital cost before the remaining lines are considered for the same treatment.
